channel.title: Said & Checked: Minnesota — AskAmerica
channel.description: What officeholders said each day from or about Minnesota, and which statements government data supports, contradicts or rules out.

item.title: Said & Checked, Minnesota, 2026-11-20: none false or contradicted, 1 unsupported, 1 unsettled (Tina Smith, Chuck Grassley)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsupported and Unsettled

  • Tina Smith, U.S. Senator: “Tribal historic preservation officers estimate that the average time to complete their historic review process is 16 days, and 98 percent of projects are reviewed on time.” Unsupported. No NATHPO or tribal historic preservation officer source publishing a 16-day average or 98% on-time rate was found; the search covered the warehouse catalog, web searches and NATHPO's November 2025 release, which gives no review-time figures.
  • Chuck Grassley, U.S. Senator: “there is a road in Colorado that took 13 years to build due to Federal permitting delays; another project in Wyoming, a wind project, that waited 12 years for Federal approval; and a mine in Minnesota that took 12 years…” Unsettled. A Colorado Politics op-ed says Interstate 70's expansion took 13 years of environmental review before work began, and the Permitting Council's page for the Chokecherry and Sierra Madre wind project in Wyoming shows it proposed in 2008 with a federal decision in 2012 and later phase approvals; neither project was confirmed as the one meant, and the 12-year wait is not established.

6 statements by 2 officeholders. 4 checked: 2 supported, 1 unsettled, 1 unsupported · 2 not checkable.
